hints.title: Compute Initial Rankings
hints.text: Rank teams by points descending and name ascending using ROW_NUMBER.

hints.title: Compute Updated Rankings
hints.text: Join PointsChange, compute the new points sum, and rank teams using the same ordering criteria.

hints.title: Compute Difference in Position
hints.text: Subtract the new rank from the old rank. A positive difference indicates an improved position.

hints.title: Complete SQL Query
hints.text:
```sql
WITH BeforeRank AS (
    SELECT 
        team_id,
        name,
        points,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY points DESC, name ASC) AS old_rank
    FROM TeamPoints
),
AfterRank AS (
    SELECT 
        tp.team_id,
        tp.name,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY (tp.points + pc.points_change) DESC, tp.name ASC) AS new_rank
    FROM TeamPoints tp
    JOIN PointsChange pc ON tp.team_id = pc.team_id
)
SELECT 
    b.team_id,
    b.name,
    (CAST(b.old_rank AS SIGNED) - CAST(a.new_rank AS SIGNED)) AS rank_diff
FROM BeforeRank b
JOIN AfterRank a ON b.team_id = a.team_id;
```

complexity.time: O(N log N) sorting twice for initial and updated team points
variables: N: number of teams in TeamPoints table
complexity.notes: Deterministic ranking with secondary name tiebreaker.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Updating tables destructively without maintaining before/after snapshots prevents atomic diffing.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Dual window passes calculate rank shifts in linear-logarithmic time.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Handle signed rank difference and secondary string ordering cleanly.

solutions.code:
import pandas as pd

def global_ratings_change(team_points: pd.DataFrame, points_change: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    tp = team_points.sort_values(by=['points', 'name'], ascending=[False, True]).reset_index(drop=True)
    tp['old_rank'] = tp.index + 1
    merged = team_points.merge(points_change, on='team_id')
    merged['new_points'] = merged['points'] + merged['points_change']
    merged = merged.sort_values(by=['new_points', 'name'], ascending=[False, True]).reset_index(drop=True)
    merged['new_rank'] = merged.index + 1
    res = tp[['team_id', 'name', 'old_rank']].merge(merged[['team_id', 'new_rank']], on='team_id')
    res['rank_diff'] = res['old_rank'] - res['new_rank']
    return res[['team_id', 'name', 'rank_diff']]
solutions.approach: Pandas sorting and rank diffing solution.
